Most studies optimise single buildings; cities need to know which urban-scale factors matter

36%

of global energy use comes from buildings

39%

of energy-related CO₂ emissions (2017)

Micro scale

One building: HVAC, materials, occupants. Informs building design.

Macro scale

Whole city: urban form, socioeconomics, morphology. Informs city policy. This project.

Three gaps in macro-scale research

1

Narrow variable sets

Socioeconomic, morphological and building variables are rarely studied together.

Addressed by component 1: data fusion
2

Unstructured data left out

Maps, street networks and 3D building models seldom enter energy models.

Addressed by component 1: data fusion
3

Accurate models are black boxes

Deep learning predicts well but cannot say which factor matters, or where.

Addressed by components 2 and 3: explainable AI, spatial analysis

Figures cited in Jiang et al., Energy 249 (2022).

One framework, three components, validated in New York City

Objective 1: a data-driven methodology framework
Input

Heterogeneous macro data

  • Socioeconomic tables
  • Lots, footprints, streets
  • 3D building models
Component 1

GIS-as-hub data fusion

Links tabular, geospatial and 3D data to every building through lot and census-tract keys.

Objective 2
Component 2

Explainable deep learning

Predicts EUI with deep and machine learning, then explains each factor's contribution with SHAP.

Objective 3
Component 3

GIS-based post‑engineering

Maps predictions and factor effects back onto the city to locate priority areas.

Objective 4
Output

Critical variables and where they act

  • Ranked drivers of EUI
  • Spatial hotspots
  • Evidence for policy

From 3,027 raw variables to 1,048 model-ready features for every Manhattan building

Raw featuresAfter preprocessing

PLUTO grows because categorical fields are one-hot encoded; the energy dataset supplies the EUI label only.

1Clean the labels

Box-plot outlier removal and log transform leave 4,854 buildings with reliable EUI.

2Fuse in space

Join every dataset to the building through lot (BBL) and census-tract codes.

3Add unlabelled buildings

34,456 buildings without energy data join as unlabelled samples.

4Engineer and select

One-hot encoding, then recursive feature elimination with LightGBM.

DUMSL-DNN: semi-supervised deep learning that also learns from unlabelled buildings

1

Train

k deep networks on k folds of the labelled buildings

2

Predict

Each network assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled buildings

3

Select

Pick t buildings by variance across the k models

4

Compare

Keep the update only if test error falls

5

Repeat

Iterate to the terminal condition

Dynamically updated multi-fold semi-supervised learning (DUMSL). Network settings from a two-round grid search. Jiang et al., Energy 249 (2022), Fig. 2 and Algorithm I.

What we found, and what we built

Three findings

30%Urban form matters beyond the building

3D factors carry about 30% of explanatory power; shading from neighbours shifts energy use by 5–10%

Pre-1965Age and type define the hotspots

Old commercial stock is the clearest high-EUI signal, concentrated in identifiable clusters

90 m, FAR 9Morphology has workable thresholds

Where height distribution and density have the least influence on energy use

Two methodological contributions

GIS hubA framework that fuses city data to every building

3,027 raw features from energy, building, census and 3D sources; 26 morphological and 24 2D/3D factors per building

−9.4%Semi-supervised deep learning for data-scarce cities

DUMSL-DNN learns from buildings without energy records, so partial data can still cover the whole stock

Why it matters

It shows where to retrofit first and what form to aim for at the design stage, at the scale of a whole city: 818,199 buildings.

Practical value: four implications for planning and energy policy

Target the pre-1965 stock first

Old commercial buildings in clusters A–E and old residential buildings in B–D: upgrade equipment, adjust business hours, add renewables, fund retrofits, upgrade to LEED criteria.

Energy (2022)

Set morphology guidance at the early design stage

Building height distribution near 90 m, FAR near 9 and compactness within 0.32–0.48 are where these factors' influence on energy use is smallest.

J. Building Engineering 85 (2024)

Put 3D form and shading into city energy models

3D factors carry about 30% of explanatory power and shading 5–10%; 2D-only models miss them.

J. Building Engineering 97 (2024)

Data-scarce cities can still model every building

Semi-supervised learning uses buildings without energy records, so cities with partial benchmarking can map the whole stock.

Energy (2022)
